author: Capitol News
title: East Lansing Police Department seeks public input for accreditation renewal
text:
Erik Altmann, mayor | City of East Lansing
Erik Altmann, mayor | City of East Lansing
The East Lansing Police Department (ELPD) is undergoing a review to renew its accreditation with the Michigan Association of Chiefs of Police (MACP). On December 10, an assessment team will visit the ELPD to collect feedback from both department employees and members of the community.
Community members and ELPD staff can share their comments with the assessors between 12:30 p.m. and 2 p.m. on December 10 by calling (517) 319-6916 or emailing Lt. Scot Sexton at [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection). Each phone comment is limited to five minutes and must focus on how the agency meets the commission’s standards. The standards can be reviewed online at https://cityofeastlansing.com/MACPaccreditation, in person at ELPD headquarters at 409 Park Lane, or by contacting Lt. Sexton directly. Anonymous comments are accepted but will not be included in the final report.
During their visit, assessors from the Michigan Law Enforcement Accreditation Commission will evaluate all aspects of ELPD’s operations, including policies, management practices, procedures, and support services. To earn accreditation, ELPD must meet 128 specific standards set by the commission.
Accreditation is a voluntary process that demonstrates a police agency’s commitment to professional excellence and adherence to best practice standards in law enforcement within Michigan.
Matt Silverthorn, Accreditation Program Director for MACP, explained the assessment process: “The assessment team is composed of law enforcement practitioners from similar Michigan law enforcement agencies. The assessors will review written materials, interview agency members and visit offices and other places where compliance with the standards can be observed. Once the assessors complete their review of the agency, they will report to the full commission, which will then decide if the agency is to be granted accredited status.”
If granted, accreditation remains valid for three years. During this period, ELPD must submit annual reports confirming continued compliance with accreditation standards.
Those interested in more information about MACP or wishing to provide written comments about ELPD’s compliance may contact MACP’s Law Enforcement Accreditation Commission at 3474 Alaiedon Pkwy, Suite 600, Okemos, MI 48864 or email [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection).
